scope: Proposition 4.1 (Sparse packet estimate) of the manuscript “Endpoint convergence for the planar Schrodinger equation” (preprints/Endpoint-convergence-for-the-planar-Schrodinger-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 080 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 68d6affc8c3cc3bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant cs > 0 with the following property. Fix τ0 > 0, and let Lτ0 ≤ D ≤ L. Let U be a finite packet array of the form (2.2), with coefficient vector c, and let µ be a nonnegative measure such that µ(B(z, r)) ≤ mr2 (r ≥ 1), supp µ ⊂ {|t| ≤ CL2 }. Assume the packet sparsity condition (2.4), with M = 100, for every label with nonzero coefficient. Then X q a unit lattice cube µ(q)2/3 sup q |U|2 ≲τ0 m2/3 L4/3 D−cs ∥c∥2 ℓ2 . (4.1) Only finitely many uniform profile derivative bounds, depending on τ0, are required. Conse- quently the same assertion holds for any prescribed finite set of field derivatives, provided the original profiles have sufficiently many bounded derivatives. Fixed enlargements of the time range and restriction to a submeasure are allowed. The exponent cs is independent of τ0; the implicit constant and the required differentiability need not be.
